scenario.title: Effective policy, item choices and shared defaults
situations: The user wants extra verification or approval for one change.
A team wants every future change to follow a new rule.
A posture change is refused because claims or evidence already exist.
scenario.current: Research trace; requirements and source paths need live proof.
questions: Resolver and guard code plus docs were inspected; individual mutation guards were not executed.
Which current UI controls explain item scope versus shared-default scope before save?
Command nodes, when present, were checked with installed CLI --help only; this proves parser/help availability, not serving-control-plane capability or successful execution.

lessons.title: One item is different from future defaults
lessons.when: When the user requests stronger checks or says only this change versus every future change.
lessons.need: An allowed item posture changes this item. Project testing/delivery defaults, universe workflow approval defaults and publishing a workflow version have wider scope. Existing item pins do not silently move.
lessons.surface: Workflows settings; workflow function reference; item-posture refusal
lessons.gap: Review question: should JOURNEYS add a change-scope prompt when the user says always or only this time, before choosing the write surface?

lessons.title: Consume resolved policies
lessons.when: Before authoring File Budget/path claims or entering a gated work phase.
lessons.need: Read effective_policies from workflows.item.get. File Budget, path claims and path survey are distinct axes; posture can tighten only permitted choices.
lessons.surface: Agent operation home; intake path closure; central resolver
lessons.gap: Review question: should public workflow help explain these choices at the moment a policy is proposed, rather than describing them as universal onboarding steps?

lessons.title: Respect existing evidence when changing policy
lessons.when: When amending or clearing an item posture after a claim, QA result or pending approval exists.
lessons.need: A selected verification method/plan, live claim or open approval may prevent clearing a choice. Use the named recovery; never erase history to make the change fit.
lessons.surface: Per-key posture guards and composed refusal recovery
lessons.gap: The technical refusal exists. Review question: should FIRST-USER 35 require a plain affected-record explanation and the exact safe next step?
